title: Embeddable website chatbot with lead capture
tagline: A chat widget you add to any website with one script tag: it answers from the site's own pages, streams the reply, and turns interested visitors into leads.
pitch: I built a chat widget that a business adds to its website with one line of code. It reads the site's own pages, so it answers visitors' questions from what the company actually says, with a link to the page, and it says so when the site does not cover the question. When a visitor shows buying interest, or asks something the site cannot answer, the widget offers a short contact form and the lead goes to the sales team with the whole conversation attached.
problem: Most visitors leave a website without finding their answer and without leaving a contact. A contact form asks for effort before giving anything back, and live chat needs a person online. A generic chatbot answers from its own memory, so it invents prices and policies the business never published.
solution: A small service and a JavaScript widget for a fictional office-furniture supplier. The service crawls the website, splits each page into sections and indexes them. A visitor's question is matched to the most relevant sections, a language model writes a short answer from those sections only, and the answer is streamed to the widget word by word with links to the source pages. A lead detector watches for buying interest and for questions the site cannot answer, then the widget shows a contact form. Leads are stored with the conversation and sent to a CRM by a signed webhook.
features: One script tag embeds the widget on any site; its styles are isolated from the host page
Answers come from the website's own pages, with links to the page and section used
Replies are streamed word by word over server-sent events
Refuses politely when the site does not cover the question, instead of guessing
Detects buying interest and offers a contact form inside the chat
Stores each lead with the conversation and sends it to a CRM through a signed webhook
Works offline with a built-in mock model; switches to OpenAI or a local model with one setting
Limits on origin, request rate and message size protect the owner's API bill

stack.name: Python 3.12 + FastAPI
stack.role: The service: chat endpoint, lead endpoint, admin page, and it serves the widget file.
stack.why: Async support makes streaming simple, and request validation comes for free.

stack.name: Vanilla JavaScript widget
stack.role: The chat bubble and panel a visitor sees on the website.
stack.why: No framework and no build step keeps the file small and lets it load on any site without conflicts.

stack.name: Server-sent events (SSE)
stack.role: Carries the answer from the server to the widget as it is written.
stack.why: It is plain HTTP, passes through proxies, and is simpler to host than WebSockets for one-way streaming.

stack.name: BM25 + sentence embeddings (fastembed)
stack.role: Finds the page sections that match a question.
stack.why: Keyword search catches product names and codes, meaning search catches paraphrases; both run on CPU.

stack.name: OpenAI-compatible chat API
stack.role: Writes the answer from the retrieved sections.
stack.why: The same code talks to OpenAI or to a local model through Ollama.

stack.name: SQLite
stack.role: Stores conversations, leads and unanswered questions.
stack.why: One file, no server to run, enough for one website's chat traffic.

workflow.detail: The crawler reads the site's sitemap, downloads each page and keeps the main text, dropping menus, footers and scripts.
Each page is split at its headings into sections. Every section is indexed for keyword search and for meaning search.
The widget sends the question and the conversation so far to the chat endpoint.
The service checks the calling website, the request rate and the message size before any model is called.
The question is matched to the most relevant sections. If nothing is relevant enough, the bot says the site does not cover it.
The model writes a short answer from the retrieved sections, and each piece is sent to the widget as it is produced, followed by the source links.
Buying interest, a request for a person, or an unanswered question makes the widget show a contact form.
The lead is saved with the conversation and posted to the CRM webhook with a signature the receiver can verify.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal: A repository that runs, a demo website to chat about, and a searchable index of its pages.

steps.text: Create the repository skeleton, the virtual environment and pinned requirements
Write the demo website: a fictional office-furniture supplier with about 12 pages
Write the crawler: sitemap, robots.txt, same-site links, HTML to clean text
Split pages into sections by heading, keeping the page title, URL and anchor
Build a BM25 keyword index as the baseline and search it from the command line

phases.outcome: A git repository with pinned dependencies, a 14-page demo website for a fictional office-furniture supplier (52 sections, about 1,600 words, generated by a script), a crawler that reads a live site or a folder and drops menus, footers, cookie banners and scripts, 66 passages split by heading, and keyword, meaning and hybrid search from the command line.

phases.name: Chat engine
phases.goal: A question goes in and a streamed, grounded answer with sources comes out, on the mock model.

steps.text: Add meaning search with embeddings and a hybrid mode that merges both rankings
Add the scope gate that refuses questions the site does not cover
Write the mock provider: a deterministic answer built from the retrieved sentences
Write the OpenAI-compatible provider with streaming, a token cap and cost tracking
Handle follow-up questions by using the previous question during retrieval
Expose the chat as a server-sent events endpoint and save conversations in SQLite

phases.outcome: A question now produces a streamed answer with links to the website sections it came from. Search runs in three modes (keywords, meaning, hybrid by reciprocal rank fusion), a scope gate refuses questions the site does not cover, follow-up questions such as 'and express?' reuse the previous question, and conversations are saved in SQLite. Two answer writers exist: an offline mock that quotes the matching sentences, and an OpenAI-compatible one with streaming, a token cap and cost tracking. The chat is served as server-sent events at POST /api/chat; on the mock the first word arrived after about 20 ms.

phases.name: Lead capture
phases.goal: Interested visitors are detected, their details are stored and the sales team is notified.

steps.text: Write the lead-intent detector: rules that always run, plus a tool the model can call
Add the lead endpoint with validation, consent and the conversation attached
Pick up an email address a visitor types directly into the chat
Send each lead to a webhook with an HMAC signature and retries
Add an admin view of leads and unanswered questions, protected by a token, with CSV export

phases.name: Widget and guards
phases.goal: The widget works on a real page in a real browser, and the service protects itself.

steps.text: Write the widget: launcher, panel, streamed replies, source links, lead form, saved session
Embed it in the demo website and serve everything with one command
Add the origin allow-list, rate limit, message-size cap and daily message budget
Drive the widget in a headless browser and take a screenshot

phases.name: Quality
phases.goal: Measured numbers for search, refusals, lead detection and speed.

steps.text: Write labelled evaluation sets: site questions, off-topic questions, lead and non-lead messages
Measure retrieval for keyword, meaning and hybrid search and pick the default
Set the refusal threshold on one half of the questions and report on the other half
Measure lead-detection precision and recall
Measure time to first word and the widget's file size

phases.name: Verification and docs
phases.goal: A stranger can clone it, run it and trust the numbers.

steps.text: Run the full test suite offline with no key
Run the quick start from a clean clone
Run the real-model check and record its cost
Write the README with a diagram, real output and the results table
Complete the dashboard entry: decisions, client questions, concepts, limits
